A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 33 pages of each version, including equations, figures, and appendices, support comparison; relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: v2 Section 7 reports original numerical simulations comparing counterfactual estimation errors and an illustrative application of the overlap test.

after.justification: v3 Section 6 and Appendix G retain original simulations and add overlap-test validation and robustness experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 and the PCR point estimator are retained. However, the revised alpha(delta) confidence radius changes the numerical threshold specified for the non-asymptotic overlap test in v2 Section 6.1 and v3 Section 5.1.

E1.justification: v3 expands evaluation to imperfect recommendation following and violations of linear span inclusion in Appendix G. Section 6.1 also evaluates populations both satisfying and violating unit overlap, substantially broadening the synthetic test scenarios.

E2.justification: The matched comparisons retain Algorithm 1 versus synthetic control without incentives, both using adaptive PCR from Agarwal et al. (2023). The added robustness studies vary conditions for Algorithm 1 rather than introducing additional comparison methods.

E3.justification: New protocols include 500 datasets per overlap class, 1,000 units per dataset, and empirical true-positive and false-positive rates. Appendix G introduces non-compliance and span-violation sweeps over p = 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8. These supplement the retained original simulation settings.

E4.justification: v3 adds systematic validation of the asymptotic overlap test and robustness analyses examining ignored recommendations and violations of Assumption 3.2. These directly test important behavioral and modeling assumptions. The original latent-dimension and belief-strength analyses remain.

E5.justification: The retained plots still report averages over 50 runs with one-standard-deviation bands. New Figures 4–5 also report 50 runs but label their bands as one standard error, adding a different uncertainty summary without a stated increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: v3 Section 6.1 adds the confusion matrix [[475, 25], [22, 478]], TPR 0.956, and FPR 0.05. Figures 4–5 add findings of worse estimation with greater non-compliance and residual error under span violations. The original comparison curves and illustrative test statistic of approximately 2.24 are retained.

T1.justification: v3 Theorem C.1 substantively revises the PCR bound from v2 Theorem B.1: several noise terms change constants and dependence on post-intervention length, including inverse-square-root versus inverse-linear scaling. Corresponding constants change in Corollary C.2 and Theorem C.5. Most other assumptions, theorems, and proofs are retained or relocated.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: overlap is necessary, incentivized exploration establishes overlap, the approach extends to multiple interventions, and two tests assess overlap. Recommender-system terminology and added supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 Section 2.2 adds a substantive qualification of literal Bayesian rationality and discusses practical imperfect recommendation following. Appendix G links non-compliance to reduced exploration and interprets span violations as a source of persistent or increasing estimation error.

D1.justification: Appendix G specifies how to generate the new perturbations: random overrides with prior-preferred interventions and padded latent coordinates activated after intervention. The original synthetic-data generation recipe is relocated from v2 Section 7, rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: v3 adds positioning relative to causal and linear causal bandits in Appendix A, with new citations including Lattimore et al. (2016) and Varici et al. (2023). Section 1.1 distinguishes unit overlap from propensity-score overlap. Some Bayesian-persuasion background citations are removed, while the central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: related work is split, preliminary sections are renamed and restructured, and the multiple-intervention extension moves from Section 5 to Appendix D. Detailed assumptions, proofs, and simulation setup also move into appendices; the contents page is removed.

P2.justification: The TMLR format changes typography, headers, margins, and title/author layout throughout. Algorithm 2 and the latent-dimension plot move into appendices. Figures 4–5 and a displayed confusion matrix are added, while the original plots are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The systematic overlap-test validation and new compliance/span-violation experiments provide useful evidence about calibration and applicability beyond v2's demonstrations. Clearer discussion of behavioral assumptions also helps interpretation. These are targeted improvements to the support and explanation of a largely retained contribution; the revised mathematical bounds alone do not establish a quality gain.
